\markright{\textit{Figure S1.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Figure S1.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{Spectral validation of confirmed chemical identifications with variant-associated differences in thyroid tumor samples.} Sample spectra for chemicals with statistically significant differences in detection or abundance across thyroid cancer variants that passed manual spectral quality review, displayed either as mirrored plots with reference standard (sample intensity in positive y-axis, standard intensity in negative y-axis) or as non-mirrored plots without standard when reference co-elution was inadequate. Mirrored plots with co-elution of multiple fragments in both standard and sample are considered ``Level 1'' identifications (S1.1, pp. 2-23), while non-mirrored plots where multiple fragments co-elute in the sample but the standard does not show proper co-elution are considered ``Level 2'' identifications (S1.2, pp. 24-26). Asterisks (*) indicate the fragment used for statistical comparison and displayed in Figure 3 and/or Table 3. For select compounds, additional plots display isolated fragments for enhanced visualization clarity.}

\markright{\textit{Figure S2.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Figure S2.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{Spectral validation of confirmed IARC Group 1 chemical identifications in thyroid tumor samples.} Sample spectra for IARC Group 1 carcinogens identified in thyroid tumor tissue that passed manual spectral quality review, displayed either as mirrored plots with reference standard (sample intensity in positive y-axis, standard intensity in negative y-axis) or as non-mirrored plots without standard when reference co-elution was inadequate. Mirrored plots with co-elution of multiple fragments in both standard and sample are considered ``Level 1'' identifications (S2.1, pp. 27-29), while non-mirrored plots where multiple fragments co-elute in the sample but the standard does not show proper co-elution are considered ``Level 2'' identifications (S2.2, pp. 30-31). Asterisks (*) indicate the fragment used for statistical comparison and displayed in Figure 3 and/or Table 3. For select compounds, additional plots display isolated fragments for enhanced visualization clarity.}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Figure S3.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{Spectral validation of confirmed IARC Group 1 chemical identifications in non-cancer cadaver thyroid samples.} Sample spectra for IARC Group 1 carcinogens identified in non-cancer cadaver thyroid tissue that passed manual spectral quality review, displayed either as mirrored plots with reference standard (sample intensity in positive y-axis, standard intensity in negative y-axis) or as non-mirrored plots without standard when reference co-elution was inadequate. Mirrored plots with co-elution of multiple fragments in both standard and sample are considered ``Level 1'' identifications (S3.1, pp. 32-34), while non-mirrored plots where multiple fragments co-elute in the sample but the standard does not show proper co-elution are considered ``Level 2'' identifications (S3.2, p. 35). Asterisks (*) indicate the fragment used for statistical comparison and displayed in Figure 3 and/or Table 3. For select compounds, additional plots display isolated fragments for enhanced visualization clarity.}

\markright{\textit{Table S1}}

\begin{landscape}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Table S1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{The full library of xenobiotic chemicals employed for chemical annotation and identification.} The library of 710 confirmed xenobiotic chemicals employed for chemical identification. All chemicals besides those which were purchased as part of a mixture with variable concentrations were present in pooled reference plasma at a concentration of 0.47 ng/mL. There are 710 total unique chemicals (i.e., unique CAS numbers), but for some chemicals, there are multiple fragments and/or retention times from different standards used for annotation and identification, thus resulting in 892 total rows in the table. The column "Target RT (min)" refers to the library retention time for the given chemical. The individual $m/z$ columns indicate typical fragments observed for the given chemical. \textit{† Both an endogenous and exogenous (xenobiotic) chemical; ‡ Additional fragments used for validation besides those listed in $m/z_0$--$m/z_3$.}}
